answer: A registry can require each agent to bond a unique hardware attestation before it may transact: the device key is ferrous-bound to one machine, so cloning the identity means buying new hardware rather than copying a file. A prism of independent verifiers then checks that the same attestation has not been reused across accounts, and a marble ledger records each binding permanently. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must therefore pay for a thousand devices and pass a thousand independent checks, which turns a cheap copy attack into an expensive, easily spotted purchase.
